title: Key transit routes
steps: From Haneda (HND): Tokyo Monorail to Hamamatsucho (≈13 min, {{fact:tokyo-monorail-haneda-519-yen}}) or Keikyu Line to Shinagawa (11–14 min, {{fact:keikyu-haneda-shinagawa-327-yen}}) — both tap in/out with an IC card, no reservation needed.
From Narita (NRT): Keisei Skyliner to Nippori/Ueno ({{fact:keisei-skyliner-2470-yen}}) is the fastest option; the JR Narita Express (N'EX) runs direct to Tokyo Station for a similar fare.

Getting around daily: tap an IC card (Suica/PASMO) at every gate on JR, Tokyo Metro, and Toei Subway — no separate tickets needed. The JR Yamanote Line loop connects the major hub stations (Tokyo, Shinjuku, Shibuya, Shinagawa, Ueno, Ikebukuro); Metro and Toei fill in everywhere else.

For a food-focused, point-to-point trip, pay-as-you-go IC card fares are usually cheaper than a multi-day subway pass — the pass excludes JR (including the Yamanote loop), so it only pays off with 5+ Metro/Toei-only rides a day.
Group of six: no special logistics — Tokyo's rail network runs frequently enough that splitting across train cars at rush hour is normal and nothing to plan around.
